checks: Re-derived with my own script (checks/q17/chk_core_null.py, same s77_lib loader, pbcor Xb4d, 1.05" beam, r=1" apertures): ridge red 180-320 = 0.246 Jy km/s (HCN), 0.196 (HCO+); lobe blue 0.321 / 0.206. Agree with s104b (0.246/0.321, 0.196/0.206). Core at ridge 2.95 / 6.2, lobe 0.62 / 1.32 also agree. Field sigma 0.025/0.032 Jy km/s. The ridge-vs-lobe ratio 0.8 and equal |v| are reproduced.

Geometry and M18 Table-1 offsets (OF-Red 3.57" at PA 357 from M18 S; South-OF-Blue 2.29" at PA 194) look right. The ridge sits where M18 OF-Red is, so detection in 1-0 supports its reality. The pixel-level mass/Mdot arithmetic follows from the lobe scaling and I accept it as scaled, not measured.

NOT adequately tested: the noise is the field sigma (random apertures >=3.5" away), but the wing flux sits on top of the brightest Bridge core (core 3-6 Jy km/s in the aperture), where deconvolution residuals, baseline error and spectral-leakage scale with core brightness and are much larger than field noise. My core-matched check shows the red wing (180-320) is positive on average in all bright pixels while the blue wing is ~0: HCN mean red/blue in pixels with core 2-4: 0.072/0.012; 4-8: 0.092/0.002; >8: 0.114/-0.002 (sd of red per bin 0.04-0.08). HCO+ 4-8: 0.057/0.017; >8: 0.094/0.015. So a red-skewed wing exists wherever the core is bright (N nucleus red wing 0.12 at core 10, ridge 0.246 at core 2.9). The ridge is only ~+0.15 above this population (~2 sigma of its scatter), so '9.7 sigma versus field noise' is not the right significance for 'ridge is a distinct feature'. The red-skew could be Bridge/N-nucleus kinematics or imaging residuals; the claim that it is a counter-lobe of S cannot yet be separated from this.

The worker's own rotation-null (s77g) and core-peak velocity (-1 km/s) argue against simple Bridge rotation; I agree on that. But the 'Bridge streaming / N red-only flow' alternatives are dismissed using collinearity (admitted non-discriminant) and a CO-axis argument, not tested against the red-skew population above.

Literature link missing: Pereira-Santaella+2024 (JWST CO v=1-0, in the card) report S-nucleus outflow emission above AND below the disk to r~250 pc, i.e. an observed bipolar structure, with a temperature gradient >40 K to <15 K. This is independent support for bipolarity (and lower excitation at larger radius, relevant to the ridge's lower r31 at 640 pc) but is not used. Also Michiyama+2018 'two-phase' result (dense fraction rises toward largest velocity) is not compared with ridge wing/core.

fixes.what: Core-brightness-matched null for the ridge wing. Build maps of the 180-320 km/s red and blue wing flux and the core flux at the common 1.05" beam over the whole Bridge/nuclear region; model the red and blue wing as functions of local core flux (and of distance to N and S), fit on pixels excluding the ridge, and report the ridge excess over that relation with an empirical scatter-based error (not field sigma). Repeat in the mirrored blue window (blue wing vs core) to see whether the red skew is genuinely one-sided.
fixes.why: Wing residuals scale with core brightness; my check shows red wing is on average +0.07-0.11 Jy km/s for core>2 while blue is ~0, so the ridge is only ~2 sigma above that population. Without this the 9.7/6.1 sigma and the ratio to the lobe (which sits on a faint core) are not comparable apertures.
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Compare to control apertures of matched continuum/core brightness; check that the wing is real in individual channels (channel maps at +200..+300 km/s, 2-3 consecutive channels at >3 sigma spatially coherent, not at the same pixels as the core peak); test baseline order and window choice (baseline fit at both ends of the band, +/-900 km/s) and report the ridge flux vs baseline choice.

fixes.what: Channel-map evidence: show the 3.9 MHz-channel (or 2-channel binned) maps at +150..+350 km/s in both lines and the same maps at -150..-350, with N, S, ridge, lobe marked; check ridge persists in each independent velocity bin and in the Xb4b (0.25") and tapered/Xb4f data at coarser beam if it is detected there (flux recovery vs beam).
fixes.why: A claim of a counter-lobe needs the feature to be coherent across independent channels and to survive different resolutions; this is currently a single windowed map at one beam.
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Moment-0 in sub-windows (+180..230, 230..280, 280..330) with ridge flux in each; compare with the lobe in mirrored sub-windows (the worker did partial sub-window fluxes; show them and the shape of the velocity profile at each side, i.e. peak velocity and width ratio).

fixes.what: Confront the N-flow / Bridge alternatives quantitatively with the red-skew population: predict, for each alternative (S counter-lobe, N red-only outflow, Bridge shear/streaming between nuclei at 250 km/s), the ridge flux, <v>, and where the wing should peak, then test (e.g. does the red wing in the nuclear Bridge scale with distance from N vs from S; is there red wing at N's far side?). Report a likelihood-type comparison, not only collinearity.
fixes.why: The verdict 'most consistent with counter-lobe' rests on equal |v|, similar HCN/HCO+ and flux 0.8, but a red-skewed wing also exists near N where no S counter-lobe is expected; those matching properties may be common to all red wing gas in the Bridge.
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Make explicit the discriminating observables (position vs S and vs N, |v| vs radius, line ratio, width) and test each against all three hypotheses with the same apertures; state which are non-discriminating.

fixes.what: Treat the 1.7x radial asymmetry and the lower r31 as a test of the counter-lobe hypothesis: give the expected r31 and size from Pereira-Santaella+2024 (outflow cooling to <15 K at 250 pc) and from M18's CO R32/10 gradient, and say whether 3-2/1-0 =0.23 at the ridge vs 0.6 at the lobe (1.5-2 sigma) is a real difference. Quote the M18 beam (~2") and the matching of the 1-0 flux to our r, and propagate the 1-0 flux error (25%) and the 3-2 residual systematic into the r31 error; if not matched, say r31 is a limit.
fixes.why: The text calls 1.5-2 sigma 'unexplained', yet that difference is the only physical discriminator of the counter-lobe from heated Bridge gas; at 1.5-2 sigma it should be stated as not significant, and the lobe-scaled mass assumes the same excitation.
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Matched-beam smoothing of the 3-2 cube to the 1-0 beam (~2"), aperture on the published 1-0 centroid, then RADEX with the ratio as a constraint to give n/T intervals and a mass range rather than scaling from the lobe.

fixes.what: Mass/outflow rate: state mass, Mdot and momentum for the ridge as lobe-scaled and tentative; report the dependence on inclination and X(HCO+), and compare to M18's HCN-based outflow mass if the card allows. Remove 'bipolar total 1.5x lobe' as a result unless the null test above survives.
fixes.why: The ridge mass inherits the unverified excitation and the not-yet-validated wing flux.
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Give the range with its dominant systematics, mark confidence 'low-moderate', and avoid derived numbers whose input detection is not yet validated against the matched-core null.

notes_for_questioner: New questions: (1) Why is the red wing (+180..+320) systematically positive in all bright Bridge/nuclear pixels while the blue is not? Is the N nucleus itself a red-skewed source (N outflow or Bridge streaming) and how much of the 'ridge' is its extension? (2) Does the JWST CO v=1-0 bipolar outflow of Pereira-Santaella+2024 extend to 640 pc in the red direction, and what is its velocity sign structure? (3) Is there a CO(2-1)/CO(3-2) or other-line counterpart of the ridge in the Xb47/Xb4f cubes at coarse beam to test flux recovery? (4) Is the ridge present in the H13CN or CS/SO windows (opacity and shock check) at a level that would discriminate shocked outflow gas from quiescent Bridge gas?
